turn_text: So I think, as I said, I love this community and I have been so privileged to work here, raise my family here. I've gotten to know people all through some of the community boards I've sat on in the community organizations I've worked in. I've gotten to know people all across the community. And like everybody else here, I lived through that terrible wrenching loss of our textile companies here back in the 1990s and early 2000s. And I saw what it did to families, people who lost their jobs, people who had great jobs for a long time, all of a sudden were out of work, didn't have the kinds of skills they needed to get good jobs. We really had to find our footing as a community to figure out how we could rebuild. And I saw people struggling to make ends meet. I saw people who had to leave this community to go find jobs elsewhere. I saw the decline of our downtown. And at the law firm, I was a partner, and I saw that it was harder for us to attract the best and the brightest to come to Greensboro because we were really struggling. And through involvement with United Way and CCJ, I saw what happened when our schools were underfunded. And I saw how tough it was not just to educate our kids, but to retain good teachers. And I also saw what happened to kids from disadvantaged homes when they started kindergarten. If they'd never been exposed to any preschool, they were already behind their peers. And I had my own struggles. When my youngest daughter was diagnosed with a chronic illness, I had to, I fought with our insurance company. They gave me the runaround because they didn't want to cover the life-saving medication that she needed. And it really made me think about what do other people go through, because I know how many people were going through such tough times with the loss of so many jobs here. I have to say that my faith tradition has instilled in me the obligation to help other people and to try to make our world and more specifically our community a better place. So I really looked for opportunities to help this community grow and regain its footing and to try to have a positive impact.
